geo.label: Fed on hold; minutes say high for longer while the curve prices the peak
parts: Macro Stance

The US goes into the Thanksgiving break priced for a soft landing that the data have only half delivered. October's flat headline CPI with core at a two-year low [[n1825]] and the 0.5% slide in producer prices [[n1831]] built the case that the hiking cycle is over. Barron's, however, read the FOMC minutes as a consensus that rates need to stay high [[n0606]], and Reuters reported Wall Street closing lower as the minutes revealed a cautious approach [[n0148]]. The real economy is cooling underneath: existing-home sales sank to a 13-year low in October [[n1870]], and Fannie Mae now expects weaker consumer spending to tip the economy into a mild recession in 2024 [[n1888]]. We stay Mixed: disinflation is genuine, growth is fading, and equities have already banked the benign half of that mix.
Rates & Curve

The 10Y closed at 4.42% and the 2Y at 4.89%, leaving 10Y-2Y at -47 bps and 10Y-3M at -112 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-22). Over 20 observations the 10Y fell 53 bps from 4.95% while the 2Y fell 19 bps from 5.08%, so the spread moved -34 bps: an inverted curve in a bull flattening move, with the long end doing the work as term premium bled out. The last five observations show -11 bps on the 10Y but only -1 bps on the 2Y, which says the front end has stopped pricing hikes without yet committing to cuts. Three-month bills at 5.54% still out-yield every other point on the curve, so cash competes with duration. The WSJ asked where the foreign buyers of Treasury debt have gone [[n0192]]; if they do not return, supply caps how far the long end can rally from here.
New / Most Important

The most important signal of the week was how little the market paid for good news. Nvidia's revenue tripled [[n0643]], yet the stock fell 2.46% to 487.16 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22). Goldman says hedge-fund bets on US stocks are the most crowded ever [[n0615]], and the VIX at 12.85 index points, down 36.35% over 20 sessions, leaves almost no insurance in the system. The S&P 500 closed at 4,556.62 index points, up 8.83% over 20 sessions and 1.19% over five, yet Seeking Alpha counts 471 days without a record close [[n1926]], so the index is pressing into a zone where crowded books either chase or sell. With US cash markets shut for Thanksgiving [[n0839]], the next liquid test comes with holiday-thinned volumes, which tends to exaggerate moves in both directions.
Playbook ✓

Action: hold duration in the belly, where the 5Y at 4.44% captures most of the rally potential, and keep equity beta at neutral rather than adding at the highs; prefer quality cash generators to crowded momentum. Trigger to add risk: the 2Y breaking below 4.89% faster than the 10Y, a bull steepening that would mean cuts are being priced for reasons equities can survive. Trigger to cut risk: a VIX move back toward 20.19, its level 20 sessions ago, or a rebound in the DXY from 103.92 index points after its 2.45% 20-session fall. What changes the call: an upside inflation surprise that validates the minutes' higher-for-longer message and pushes the curve into a bear flattening.

geo.label: ECB on hold; cut talk 'premature' as German fiscal space shrinks
parts: Macro Stance

Europe's equity rally has outrun its economy. The Euro Stoxx 50 closed at 4,361.32 index points, up 7.70% over 20 sessions, and the DAX at 15,994.73, up 8.58% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23), while euro-area GDP dipped 0.1% in Q3 [[n1074]]. Germany froze government spending as its budget crisis deepened [[n1131]], turning a growth problem into a fiscal one. Mixed: lower global yields lift multiples, but the domestic growth engine is stalling.
Activity & Inflation

The ECB is leaning against the market's relief. Lagarde warned against a premature celebration on inflation [[n1127]] and de Cos called it premature to start talking about cuts [[n1112]]. The pipeline argues the other way: European Business Magazine expects German inflation to decline further as producer prices fall [[n1856]]. Activity is soft after the October PMI sat at a near three-year low [[n1065]], and the ECB warns euro-zone banks are starting to show stress as loan defaults rise [[n1134]].
New / Most Important

The new risk is fiscal tightening by accident. Reuters reports Germany's steel sector warning that the budget hole puts industry at risk [[n0819]], and the Commission has warned France over breaches of fiscal guidance [[n1128]]. That hits transition subsidies just as cyclicals price a recovery: Siemens has rallied 23.47% over 20 sessions to 149.64 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23), which shifts the burden of proof from rates to order books.
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer euro duration and quality exporters with dollar revenue over domestic German cyclicals, and keep European autos underweight. Trigger: a German budget fix that restores investment funds would justify adding cyclicals; another bank-stress warning would argue for trimming lenders. What changes the call: ECB speakers moving from 'premature' to data-dependent language on cuts.

geo.label: Targeted property support; benchmark lending rates on hold
parts: Macro Stance

China is easing by increments, not by bazooka, and markets are pricing exactly that. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,061.86 index points, up 2.46% over 20 sessions, and the Hang Seng at 17,910.84, up 5.08% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23), a recovery led by platform names while the property complex keeps leaking. Reuters reported benchmark lending rates left unchanged, as expected [[n0196]], even though consumer prices slipped back into decline [[n0171]]. Economist Yu Yongding is flagging stagflation risks [[n0228]], and Bloomberg reports a labour market weaker than official data show [[n0234]]. Mixed: support is real but rationed, and falling prices blunt each dose.
PMIs & Activity

The activity pulse is weak at the margin. Caixin's survey confirmed an October manufacturing slump [[n0168]], and exports fell for a sixth straight month even as imports rose [[n0172]]. September industrial profits extended gains on policy support [[n0167]], so margins are stabilising faster than volumes. Consumption is the swing factor: Sixth Tone asks whether the Double Eleven festival has lost its luster [[n0220]], while Miniso's earnings jumped 49% in its best quarter on rapid store expansion [[n1006]]. Value-led spending is growing; trading up is not. McKinsey's 'start of a new era' framing [[n0247]] is the bull case, and the price data remain the bear case.
Credit Impulse

Credit is being steered rather than expanded. Reuters reports that high-tech manufacturing loans are raising fears of a wave of cheap exports [[n0174]], which shows where the marginal yuan of bank lending goes: to capacity, not to households. The plumbing is under strain too. A Chinese shadow bank admitted a £30bn shortfall after management 'ran wild' [[n0249]], a reminder that trust and wealth products are the channel through which property losses reach household balance sheets. Premier Li Qiang was named head of a powerful financial body [[n0201]], and Reuters says finance veteran Zhu is to become the new forex chief [[n0236]]. Centralised control should make credit allocation more deliberate, not looser, so a broad credit impulse is unlikely before the policy machinery settles.
Property

Property policy is moving from demand-side tweaks toward direct developer support. The Business Times reports Beijing weighing unprecedented builder support with first-ever unsecured loans [[n0248]], and Shenzhen cut down payments on second homes as cities try to revive demand [[n0254]]. Analysts told Reuters a turnaround needs 'multiple levers' [[n0197]], and the WSJ says the unfinished-homes problem keeps getting bigger [[n0198]]. The New York Times describes plans to bulldoze old neighbourhoods to revive the economy [[n0183]], a quasi-fiscal construction impulse through urban renewal. Prices are still falling in more cities [[n0180]]. Unsecured lending is the line that matters: it moves the state from refinancing projects to underwriting developers themselves.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

External policy is in a thaw. Beijing approved the Broadcom-VMware merger with conditions, which the South China Morning Post read as a sign of thaw with the US [[n0777]], after a Xi-Biden meeting that China hailed despite the 'dictator' remark [[n0099]]. The PBOC and Saudi Arabia's central bank signed a swap worth $7 billion [[n0204]], and Asia Financial reports the yuan passing the euro as the second top trade currency [[n0184]]. Friction has migrated to products and routing: hybrid sales are surging at home, posing a fresh threat to foreign automakers [[n0476]], and The Economist reports Chinese companies flocking to Mexico [[n0255]]. The US criminal probe into Applied Materials' shipments to SMIC [[n0275]] shows that technology controls remain the hard edge of the relationship.
Markets & Flows

The equity split is about governance more than macro. Tencent closed at 329.20 HKD, up 14.46% over 20 sessions, and Xiaomi gained 15.57%, while Alibaba fell 5.04% over five sessions to 77.25 HKD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23). Reuters says the U-turn on the cloud spin-off lopped $20 billion off Alibaba's market value [[n0267]], analysts cut price targets by up to 25% [[n0444]], and Jack Ma reversed a plan to sell shares after the slide [[n0230]]. The yuan traded near a four-month high on firmer fixings and steadier China-US ties [[n0227]]. Offshore wrappers lag the local tape: FXI fell 3.38% and ASHR 1.37% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), so dollar-based money has not yet followed the policy headlines.
New / Most Important

The unsecured-loan proposal is the most important new fact because it changes who carries developer risk. If banks lend to builders without collateral, losses migrate onto state-bank balance sheets, and the shadow-bank channel stays exposed as a second fault line. Metals have already priced the support: the SCMP reports China demand hopes drove copper to a two-month peak [[n0215]], and copper closed at 3.78 USD/lb, up 5.90% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23). The Economist's 'How to save China's economy' [[n0252]] captures the debate: support is aimed at completion and liquidity, not at household demand, which is why consumer prices are still falling.
Playbook ✓

Action: own Hong Kong-listed platform leaders with cash returns, Tencent first, and keep metals exposure through copper miners, but stay out of developers and out of Alibaba until the restructuring path is credible. Trigger to add: formal adoption of unsecured builder loans alongside a cut in benchmark lending rates. Trigger to cut: another shadow-bank failure or a fresh leg down in home prices. ⚠ Divergence: policy headlines are turning more supportive, yet offshore China ETFs fell over five sessions and consumer prices are back in decline, so the rally in metals and Hong Kong tech is front-running a demand recovery the price data do not yet show.

geo.label: BOJ exit bets build; yen firming
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is the one major market where inflation is a regime change investors welcome. Reuters says Japan's inflation comeback is prompting investors to tear up old playbooks [[n1262]], and the Nikkei 225 closed at 33,451.83 index points, up 7.69% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), its last session before the holiday. Growth is choppy — Japan Economy Watch calls it a 'yo-yo' GDP [[n1256]] — and the Kishida cabinet's approval rating is the lowest since the LDP regained power [[n1263]], which limits fiscal follow-through after the $113 billion inflation package [[n1240]]. Bullish on domestic reflation beneficiaries; more selective on exporters.
Activity & Currency

The currency is turning. The Japan Times reports Pimco buying yen to prepare for tighter BOJ policy [[n1264]], and MarketWatch notes the previously invincible dollar sliding against the yuan and the yen [[n1268]]. Exporters already feel it: Toyota fell 4.60% over five sessions to 2,728.50 JPY and Advantest dropped 4.33% in one session to 4,570.00 JPY, while Tokyo Electron is still up 19.61% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22). Exports grew better than expected as auto shipments climbed [[n1251]], so a firmer yen is a margin issue rather than a volume shock. Reuters' Morning Bid framed the national CPI print as the release to light up holiday-thinned trade [[n1283]].
Playbook ✓

Action: favour domestic demand, banks and service exporters over large-cap manufacturers, and hedge less of the yen exposure than in prior quarters. Trigger: sticky core inflation reinforces BOJ exit pricing and the yen bid; a soft print revives the carry trade and flatters exporters again. What changes the call: a renewed dollar rebound — the DXY rose 0.32% in its latest session even after a 2.45% 20-session fall. EWJ at 62.49 USD, up 7.50% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), shows dollar-based holders have already been paid, so new entries should be currency-unhedged only on dips.

geo.label: RBA at 4.35% and warning on 'homegrown' inflation
parts: Macro Stance

Australia has the most hawkish central-bank rhetoric in the developed world and an economy beginning to feel it. The RBA lifted the cash rate 25 basis points to 4.35% [[n0016]], and Governor Bullock now calls inflation increasingly homegrown, suggesting rates will remain high [[n0086]]. The ASX 200 closed at 7,029.20 index points, down 0.62% in its latest session and up only 3.18% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23). Bearish on rate-sensitive domestic equities.
Demand & Financing

The RBA minutes cited 'growing signs' that businesses were passing on cost increases [[n0047]], and Bullock's wages warning [[n0061]] keeps another hike alive. Demand is splitting: CommBank data show consumers cutting discretionary spending but leaving room for travel and entertainment [[n0063]], and the ABC warns record Black Friday sales could precede a 'penny-pinching' Christmas [[n0089]]. Bullock's claim that haircuts and services are driving inflation was slammed as 'ridiculous' [[n0095]], but the backlash does not change the services arithmetic while record immigration lifts rents [[n0073]]. CBA closed at 102.96 AUD, down 0.81% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23).
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight domestic cyclicals and banks; keep miners as the preferred Australian exposure while iron ore holds a two-year high [[n0038]] and BHP sits on a 1.27% five-session gain. Trigger: a soft monthly CPI or a sharper consumer slowdown would let the RBA stop at the current cash rate; another services surprise raises the odds of a further hike. What changes the call: a stronger Australian dollar, which Livewire is already positioning for [[n0077]], would tighten conditions further and hurt offshore earners.

geo.label: NBP on pause; power passes to a Tusk coalition
parts: Macro Stance

Poland is the cleanest regime-change trade in Europe: a pro-EU government is assembling, EU money is unlocking and, as Gazeta.pl put it, the zloty is the strongest in years [[n1355]]. The macro base is turning up. Bankier reports the economy avoided a technical recession [[n1335]], industry finally moved back into positive territory [[n1461]], and real wages are rising at the fastest pace in years with nominal pay at a record [[n1464]]. Super Biznes reports the first rise in consumption in nine months [[n1498]]. The catch is persistence: TVN24 notes October inflation came in higher than first estimated [[n1341]], and RPP member Kotecki warns Poland has the second-highest deficit in the EU and expects a Commission reaction [[n1354]]. Bullish, with fiscal discipline as the variable to watch.
Markets

Polish assets have re-rated hard since the October 15 election. EPOL closed at 21.78 USD, up 13.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), and the Beta WIG20TR tracker at 40.33 PLN, up 6.42% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23); much of the gap is currency, since the dollar-based ETF also captures a zloty that Business Insider Polska says 'shines worldwide', with forecasts giving it plenty more room [[n1512]]. Comparic notes the euro has lost more against the zloty this year than in any year for a decade [[n1541]], and Parkiet's morning analysis describes sustained pressure on the dollar [[n1404]]. Banks led: PKO BP rose 11.21% over 20 sessions to 46.74 PLN, Pekao 9.13% and mBank 8.73%, while Orlen fell 4.25% and Tauron 3.74% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23). The latest session was a pause, with the WIG20TR tracker down 0.52%, consistent with profit-taking rather than a change of story.
Fiscal & Politics

The handover is now mechanical. Gazeta Prawna reports that Morawiecki's government will be sworn in on Monday but that the budget will be submitted by a Tusk government [[n1561]]; Rzeczpospolita says, unofficially, that Tusk's cabinet is complete with one ministry left to fill [[n1547]], and Polsat reports Tusk pointing to St Lucy's day in mid-December [[n1538]]. Morawiecki is still courting Third Way and Confederation [[n1377]], with Money.pl quoting doubts that anyone has even received an offer [[n1384]]. The money is the market story: OKO.press says it is official that €5 billion from the KPO recovery plan will flow despite unmet milestones [[n1467]], Interia says the first large transfers arrive in January [[n1471]], and WysokieNapiecie notes the Commission accepted the revised KPO with energy the biggest winner [[n1501]]. The cost side is just as concrete: Business Insider Polska tabulates how Tusk's flagship pledge would raise public-sector pay [[n1565]], and DW's press review stresses that the EU billions are not unconditional [[n1555]].
Corporate & Sectors

The corporate tape maps the political transition. Business Insider Polska reports a collapse in a state company's share price against a backdrop of big wage rises and an extra tax [[n1571]]; coking-coal miner JSW fell 12.17% in its latest session to 42.00 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23), consistent with that description, and Wyborcza reports a stalled prosecutor's probe into money siphoned out of JSW [[n1575]]. PGE is reshuffling its board as a Ziobro-linked executive departs [[n1572]], and PZU chief Beata Kozłowska-Chyła is reportedly headed to the NBP [[n1557]]. Orlen chartered a supertanker to carry Venezuelan crude to China [[n1564]] and will not take over Azoty Puławy [[n1458]]. In private names, Dino warned a large transaction may not close [[n1495]] yet is up 16.26% over 20 sessions to 441.90 PLN, and LPP's billionaire founder is gradually withdrawing [[n1503]]. CD Projekt fell 3.03% to 110.40 PLN despite announcing a Cyberpunk 2077 Ultimate Edition for this year [[n1452]], while Pepco drew a broker downgrade that cut the target by more than half [[n1417]] even as the stock rose 8.88% over five sessions.
Geopolitics & Security

Security risk is rising but contained. Al Jazeera reports Poland charged 16 people after dismantling a Russian spy ring [[n1307]], which BBC Monitoring says sought to disrupt arms supplies to Ukraine [[n1309]], and Polish counter-intelligence says it continuously tracks hostile Russian and Belarusian services [[n1513]]. Truckers' protests at the Ukrainian border have left Ukrainian drivers stranded [[n1296]], an irritant for logistics and for Warsaw's ties with Kyiv. Procurement continues — PGZ is to build a 'superradar' for the Patriot system [[n1362]] — and Interia's report that NATO has five years to be ready [[n1386]] underpins the multi-year defence line in the budget. PiS and PO both oppose EU treaty change [[n1304]], so the incoming government's pro-EU turn will be about funds and rule of law rather than deeper integration.
New / Most Important

The NBP is the new fault line. Fakty TVN reports Governor Glapiński could face the State Tribunal over the bank's bond purchases [[n1411]]; the NBP has written to the ECB to complain [[n1421]], its first deputy president calls the grounds 'trumped-up and political' [[n1403]], and Money.pl quotes the view that there is 'no room for allegations of unconstitutionality' [[n1563]]. For markets the question is the reaction function, not the legal outcome: a governor under pressure from an incoming government may resist cuts to demonstrate independence, which supports the zloty but delays relief for floating-rate borrowers. Obserwator Finansowy's argument that a higher-rate policy can support financial stability [[n1364]] reads as intellectual cover for a long pause.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay overweight Polish banks and the zloty through EPOL and the WIG20TR tracker, and avoid state-controlled energy and coal until new boards and the tax regime are known. Trigger to add: the Tusk government's confidence vote and the first KPO disbursement. Trigger to trim: a State Tribunal motion that escalates into open conflict with the NBP, or a deficit path that draws formal Commission action. Banks carry their own legal tail as law firms 'go after WIBOR', although court rulings have so far disappointed them [[n1395]]. ⚠ Divergence: the zloty and EPOL price a smooth transition and EU money, but the NBP-government clash and a pay-heavy budget point to more fiscal and institutional noise, and JSW's 12.17% drop shows how fast state-company equity can be re-priced.
Narrative

Technology remains the market's earnings anchor and its most crowded trade. XLK closed at 184.77 USD, up 13.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22). The OpenAI governance crisis ended with Sam Altman back as CEO [[n1717]] and Microsoft at a record high along the way [[n0493]], so the AI franchise survived intact.
Reported

HP forecast a downbeat first-quarter profit amid a slow PC recovery [[n0997]], the clearest sign that AI budgets are not lifting legacy hardware. Palo Alto's fiscal first-quarter results [[n0925]] kept security in the priority bucket, and PANW is up 2.72% over five sessions.
EPS Upside Watch

Goldman expects AI to shift from 'excitement' to 'deployment' in 2024 [[n0937]], which matters most for application software: ServiceNow is up 26.31% and Adobe 18.92% over 20 sessions, pricing monetisation that now has to show up in bookings and seat expansion rather than in demos.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The OpenAI saga raised platform concentration risk rather than lowering it. Microsoft's offer to absorb OpenAI staff on the same pay [[n1005]] showed how few firms really control the AI stack, and with hedge-fund crowding at a record [[n0473]] the exit door is narrow if a leader stumbles.
Narrative

Communication services is splitting into ad-funded winners and content-cost losers. XLC rose 10.00% over 20 sessions to 71.20 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), with Meta up 14.01% and Netflix 16.23%. Business Insider expects streamers to step up the ad wars in 2024 [[n1657]], and Warner Bros. cut the price of ad-supported Max [[n1699]].
Reported

Warner Music's fiscal fourth-quarter release [[n0935]] kept the music-rights compounding story intact. Brand-safety risk is live: Apple, Disney and other media companies paused advertising on X after Musk boosted an antisemitic post [[n0272]], a reminder that ad budgets move quickly to perceived safe venues.
EPS Upside Watch

Spotify's tie-up with Google's AI for recommendations [[n0983]] and United Airlines weighing passenger data to sell targeted ads [[n1732]] show where ad growth is migrating: toward first-party data. Snap, up 33.95% over 20 sessions, is the high-beta proxy for that shift.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Meta broke up its Responsible AI team [[n0955]] and the market read it as cost discipline. With Discord, Snap and X chiefs subpoenaed to testify on child exploitation [[n0462]], governance spending has been deferred, not removed, and could return as a regulatory bill.
Narrative

Financials are the quiet beneficiary of the bond rally. XLF closed at 35.27 USD, up 9.88% over 20 sessions, with Citigroup up 16.60% and Bank of America 15.97% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22); lower long yields shrink unrealised securities losses and revive capital-markets fees.
Reported

Citi is shuffling bosses in a 'difficult' management overhaul [[n0590]], and Blackstone is closing a multi-strategy fund after assets fell nearly 90% [[n0583]], evidence that alternative managers are culling rather than expanding. In Europe the ECB warns banks are starting to show stress as loan defaults rise [[n1134]].
EPS Upside Watch

Regional banks are the swing factor: KRE is up 14.96% over 20 sessions but down 1.69% over five, so the relief rally is stalling. The St. Louis Fed's map of where commercial real estate risks sit [[n1146]] is the guidance investors need before margin upside becomes credible.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Robinhood now pays 5.00% on cash [[n1583]]: deposit competition has not ended even though hikes may have. If the next phase is cuts, the banks that paid up for deposits regain margin first, which argues for owning funding-sensitive lenders over asset-sensitive ones.
Narrative

Energy is the market's disinflation donor. WTI closed at 77.10 USD/bbl, down 9.71% over 20 sessions, and XLE fell 3.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22). CNN reported oil dropping 4% on the delay to the OPEC meeting [[n1737]], though WTI finished that session down only 0.86%, exposing disagreement over who carries further cuts.
Reported

The EIA reports US gasoline prices declining on lower demand and falling crude [[n1747]], and Venezuela says it is producing 850,000 bpd and wants back its US market share [[n1046]]: more barrels into a market already doubting discipline. Brent's 5.10% five-session rebound to 81.37 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23) shows how fast a risk premium can return.
EPS Upside Watch

Upside sits with downstream margins if crude falls faster than products, but the Citgo auction nears as demand for refineries fades [[n1731]], a sign buyers will not pay for that margin. Exxon is down 4.22% and Chevron 7.40% over 20 sessions.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The Houthi seizure of a ship in the Red Sea [[n1190]] and the EIA's reminder that Hormuz is the world's most important chokepoint [[n0224]] mean the market is short geopolitical optionality just as positioning turns bearish.
Narrative

Industrials are a tale of aerospace up, agriculture down. XLI closed at 106.08 USD, up 8.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22); Boeing rose 23.73% as the FAA cleared flight tests for 737 MAX 10 certification [[n0786]], and the New York Times explains why China and Boeing still need each other [[n0793]].
Reported

Deere's 2024 guidance missed estimates and the shares tumbled [[n0715]], falling 3.11% to 370.76 USD even though fiscal-year net income surged [[n0714]]. Siemens' fourth-quarter release [[n0933]] supported a 23.47% 20-session rally in its shares.
EPS Upside Watch

Commercial aerospace is the cleanest upside: leasing giant SMBC ordered 60 A320neo jets [[n0628]] and GE hit a six-year high [[n0723]], with Airbus up 6.44% over 20 sessions. Defence adds a second leg, with Rheinmetall expecting 13-14 billion euros of revenue in 2026 [[n0651]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The UAW clinched record Detroit deals and is turning to organising Tesla and foreign automakers [[n1206]]. Labour-cost inflation is migrating from autos into the wider manufacturing base, a margin headwind that capital-goods multiples are not pricing.
Narrative

The consumer is trading down, not dropping out. TJX raised guidance again as shoppers hunt for deals [[n0927]], and Barron's calls off-price retailers big winners after Ross rose on earnings [[n0341]]; ROST is up 5.65% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22).
Reported

Lowe's missed sales estimates and cut its outlook [[n1000]], and Nordstrom's sales missed ahead of Black Friday [[n1011]], while Abercrombie raised its outlook after a 20% sales surge [[n0569]]. Home improvement and department stores are losing share to brands with momentum and to off-price channels.
EPS Upside Watch

Amazon, up 20.86% over 20 sessions to 146.71 USD, is the scaled discount channel for a value-seeking shopper. Reuters reports US retailers bracing for a tough holiday despite discounts [[n0673]], which favours platforms with logistics leverage over promotion-dependent chains.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Tesla is now a consumer-brand risk. The WSJ reports investor backlash to Musk's social-media comments [[n1622]] and Barron's says new Model Y deals may not please investors [[n0778]]; TSLA fell 2.90% to 234.21 USD, as price cuts substitute for brand pull.
Narrative

Staples have lost their defensive premium to weight-loss anxiety and grocery disinflation. XLP is up only 3.25% over 20 sessions to 70.15 USD while the S&P 500 gained 8.83% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22). Morgan Stanley lists the stocks most at risk as Ozempic patients eat less [[n0845]], and Reuters found the Wegovy craze all the rage on Q3 calls [[n0426]].
Reported

Walmart's top line expanded as consumers seek value [[n0936]], yet WMT fell 8.90% over five sessions to 154.67 USD as Business Insider reported it is ready for grocery prices to come down [[n0952]]. Target jumped more than 17% on an earnings beat even as sales fell again [[n0929]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside is narrow and sits where volume holds without promotion: Costco at 589.08 USD and Coca-Cola, up 2.12% over five sessions, keep pricing power; Nestle's 1.73% five-session gain shows Europe's defensives catching a similar bid.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Grocery deflation is good for real incomes but bad for nominal staples earnings. The sector's role as an inflation hedge flips into that of a disinflation victim, so staples are no longer the default hiding place if the cycle turns.
Narrative

Healthcare is a GLP-1 sector with a drag attached. Novo Nordisk announced a new $2.3 billion investment in France [[n1762]] and plans a manufacturing blitz as the market for its drug is expected to top $100 billion in 2030 [[n1763]]; NVO rose 7.08% over five sessions to 103.26 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22).
Reported

Medtronic reported fiscal second-quarter results [[n1004]], while Bayer's blood thinner failed against Eliquis, sinking a phase 3 trial and denting a $5B sales forecast [[n0447]]. Pipeline risk outside obesity is being repriced quickly.
EPS Upside Watch

Novo will cut Victoza output to boost Ozempic supply [[n1745]], so capacity rather than demand is the constraint. Mercer expects weight-loss drugs to drive up employers' medical costs in 2024 [[n1636]], a headwind for managed care; UnitedHealth is up only 2.56% over 20 sessions.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Senator Sanders is pressing Merck, J&J and Bristol Myers Squibb to testify on drug pricing [[n0655]]. Pricing politics may hit legacy pharma before it touches the GLP-1 leaders, and XBI's 11.15% 20-session gain shows money rotating toward biotech instead.
Narrative

Materials are pricing China's targeted support. Copper hit a two-month peak on China demand hopes [[n0215]] and iron ore holds a two-year high [[n0038]]; Freeport-McMoRan rose 9.01% over 20 sessions to 36.89 USD and Alcoa 10.65% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), while XLB gained 8.47%.
Reported

Franco-Nevada cut guidance on the Cobre Panama mine's troubles [[n0970]], a reminder that jurisdiction risk is now the binding constraint on copper supply. Fortescue approved $750 million for three green projects [[n0575]], diverting iron-ore cash into energy transition capex.
EPS Upside Watch

Lower silver output in Peru and Mexico is set to drag down global production [[n1650]], supportive for silver at 23.67 USD/oz, up 3.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22); supply discipline, not demand, is the cleaner earnings lever across metals.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Germany's steel industry warns that the budget hole puts it at risk [[n0819]]. European metals demand now depends on fiscal decisions in Berlin as much as on Beijing's property measures, so the bullish call is a China-and-supply call, not a European one.
Narrative

Real estate is a pure rates trade. XLRE rose 12.40% over 20 sessions to 36.18 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22) as the 10Y fell 53 bps, but fundamentals keep deteriorating: CNN reports US home sales on pace for the worst year since 1993 [[n1874]].
Reported

Existing-home sales fell in October as inventory remained tight [[n1868]], and Morgan Stanley expects home prices to fall in 2024 [[n1869]]. Transactions, not prices, are what have broken, which hurts brokers and lenders before landlords.
EPS Upside Watch

Activist Land & Buildings raised its stake in single-family-rental REIT Tricon, calling it 'substantially undervalued' [[n0698]]: private capital sees value in rental housing precisely because ownership is unaffordable and transactions are frozen.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Jim Chanos, the best-known short seller of data-center REITs, is closing his main hedge funds [[n0394]]. The data-center build-out is now consensus, which is usually when supply risk becomes underpriced; the trade to fade is the crowded one, not the hated one.
Narrative

Utilities sit between lower yields and a capex boom. XLU rose 5.36% over 20 sessions to 62.53 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), with Constellation Energy up 10.02% as nuclear and power-demand themes gain, while NextEra lagged at 1.79%.
Reported
NRG Energy's CEO left after the company struck a pact with Elliott [[n0503]], an activist push for capital discipline that tends to precede buybacks or asset sales rather than new build-out.
EPS Upside Watch

Data-center construction keeps spreading — Skybox began work on a massive site in southern Dallas County [[n1690]] — and MIT Technology Review describes AI making the power grid faster and more resilient [[n1736]]. Load growth is the earnings lever for regulated utilities with rate-base expansion.
⚡ Breaking Convention

NuScale was hit with an investor lawsuit [[n0762]] and SMR is down 26.57% over 20 sessions: the nuclear renaissance is a fuel and large-reactor story for now, not a small-modular one, so owning operators beats owning developers.
Narrative

European autos face a margin squeeze from Chinese competition. Reuters reports surging hybrid sales in China posing a fresh threat to foreign automakers [[n0476]], and BYD sold more than 300,000 electric cars in a month [[n0587]]. The STOXX Europe 600 autos tracker closed at 54.16 EUR, up 7.18% over 20 sessions but down 0.35% in its latest session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23).
Reported

ACEA data show new car registrations up 14.6% in October with battery-electric share at 14.2% [[n1714]], healthy volumes at weakening prices. Volvo Cars fell to a record low as Geely sold shares [[n0372]], showing how quickly a strategic holder can turn seller.
EPS Upside Watch

Stellantis and CATL plan a European factory to make cheaper EV batteries [[n0663]]; cost-down is the only route to defend margins. Renault fell 2.44% and Volkswagen 1.55% over five sessions, while BMW at 94.13 EUR remains the quality exception.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Transport & Environment warns leasing firms could flood the used market with electric cars [[n1710]], which would pressure residual values and captive-finance earnings — the least-discussed channel through which an EV price war reaches carmaker profits.
Narrative

Semis remain the AI earnings engine. SOXX closed at 515.07 USD, up 16.47% over 20 sessions, and the SOX index at 3,744.96 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22). ASML's US line is up 17.39% and TSMC's ADR 12.56% over the same span, so the rally has broadened from GPUs to the toolmakers and the foundry.
Reported

Nvidia earned five times more revenue from AI chips than from gaming GPUs [[n1009]], and diginomica highlights revenue up 200% year on year with sovereign AI clouds as the next opportunity [[n1036]]. Broadcom closed its $69 billion VMware deal after China's approval [[n0707]].
EPS Upside Watch

Marvell is expected to beat earnings estimates [[n0162]], a pending test of whether custom AI silicon broadens the winners. TSMC is weighing a next-generation fab in Japan [[n0776]], and TrendForce tracks EUV adoption at Intel, TSMC and Samsung [[n1768]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Export controls are the cap on the story. Applied Materials is under a US criminal probe over shipments to SMIC [[n0275]], Nvidia removed the 4090 card from its China website [[n0510]], and Advantest fell 4.33% in one session; China revenue is the line analysts should haircut first.

earnings_pattern.title: Margins and guidance beat sales, and an AI beat is no longer enough
parts: Rewarded

Companies that protected margin with lean inventory were paid handsomely. Target jumped more than 17% after a big earnings beat even as sales fell [[n0929]]; Gap rose 30% on its new CEO's revival effort [[n0305]]; Abercrombie raised its outlook after sales surged 20% [[n0569]]; and Burlington surged as off-price retailers kept winning [[n0585]]. In Europe, caterer Elior jumped on its first annual core profit since COVID [[n1026]]. The common thread is self-help: cost cuts, tighter stock and a value proposition that wins share from weaker rivals.
Punished

Guidance cuts were punished without mercy. Deere tumbled on 2024 guidance below estimates [[n0715]], Lowe's dropped after missing sales and cutting its outlook [[n1000]], and Kingfisher issued its second profit warning in two months [[n1034]]. HP's downbeat first-quarter forecast [[n0997]] hit the PC complex, and Siemens Gamesa's turnaround plan underwhelmed [[n0658]]. Even a record quarter was sold: Nvidia slipped 2.46% after results (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22).
Pattern

The market pays for profit quality and forward visibility, not for top-line beats. Margin expansion from inventory discipline is rewarded; volume-led businesses with cyclical end markets are punished on guidance. That is late-cycle behaviour: investors assume revenue slows in 2024 and pay only for companies able to grow earnings anyway. Plug Power's accounting warning [[n0648]] and its 44.05% 20-session collapse mark the tail for balance-sheet risk.
Attention into EPS

BofA's Keith Banks says the next sustained growth in earnings could come in the second half of 2024 [[n0950]], and Goldman forecasts a 6% S&P 500 return in 2024 [[n0139]]. Morgan Stanley's list of stocks for safe, high-quality earnings heading into a volatile 2024 [[n0829]] captures the institutional mood: quality over beta. Attention now concentrates on a handful of AI and off-price names, which raises the bar for every subsequent print in those groups.
Playbook

Action: buy guidance-raisers with margin levers on post-earnings weakness, and avoid cyclicals guiding down into 2024. Trigger: holiday trading — Retail Dive's Black Friday and Cyber Monday preview [[n0149]] sets the bar — will decide whether off-price leadership extends into the new year. What changes the call: a broadening of top-line growth that would make volume cyclicals cheap rather than traps.

underowned.title: Small caps behind the megacap crowd
parts: Attention Gap

Goldman flags hedge-fund crowding at a new record in popular positions [[n0473]], almost all of it in large caps, while small caps get a fraction of the attention; Interactive Investor's case for small-caps in four charts [[n1057]] is a rare voice. The Russell 2000 closed at 1,795.54 index points, up 8.73% over 20 sessions but down 0.32% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22).
Exposure & Risk
IWM at 178.13 USD is the most rate-sensitive slice of US equity: heavier floating-rate debt and thinner margins. The risk is that a hawkish data surprise hits small caps first and hardest.
Trigger to Watch

The 2Y yield: a sustained move below 4.89% that reflects cuts being priced would lift refinancing-heavy small caps more than megacaps. Business Insider's interview with 2023's best small-cap fund manager [[n0581]] shows stock pickers are already hunting there.

underowned.title: Uranium and the nuclear fuel chain
parts: Attention Gap

NZ Funds says its uranium bet has returned over 300% [[n1761]], yet uranium remains a niche allocation outside specialist funds. URA closed at 28.81 USD, up 8.92% over 20 sessions and 4.20% over five, while Cameco rose 14.65% over 20 sessions to 45.00 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22).
Exposure & Risk

URA and Cameco carry exposure to fuel prices and long-term contracting; the risk sits in the reactor-developer end, where NuScale's investor lawsuit [[n0762]] shows how far expectations can run ahead of execution. Centrus is down 3.79% over 20 sessions.
Trigger to Watch

Evidence that data-center load growth is turning into firm power contracts — MIT Technology Review's account of AI reshaping the grid [[n1736]] — would pull uranium from thematic niche into utility-procurement mainstream.

underowned.title: EM sovereign debt after the early hikers
parts: Attention Gap

The FT argues emerging-market central banks may be trumping the Fed and the ECB [[n1129]], and Schroders calls emerging Europe the standout EM region of 2023 [[n1133]]. Yet EM debt stays an afterthought next to US megacaps; EMB rose 5.61% over 20 sessions to 85.16 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22).
Exposure & Risk

EMB holds dollar sovereign debt, so it gains from falling Treasury yields and a softer dollar. The risk is idiosyncratic: Turkey raised rates to 40% [[n0164]], and Argentina's stocks and bonds swing on Milei's 'chainsaw' pledges [[n1932]].
Trigger to Watch
A DXY that keeps falling from 103.92 index points would extend EM local and dollar debt gains; a dollar rebound reversing the 2.45% 20-session decline is the signal to cut.

underowned.title: Central-bank gold while equities run
parts: Attention Gap

Gold sits at 1,993.30 USD/oz, down 0.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23), ignored while equities rally. Yet Money.pl reports the NBP expanding its bullion reserves [[n1477]], and Standard Chartered asks whether the world faces a new gold standard [[n1598]].
Exposure & Risk

GDX at 29.25 USD, up 3.76% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), gives leveraged exposure to the metal. The risk is the dollar: Reuters had gold dropping below $2,000 as the dollar gained and yields pared losses [[n1880]].
Trigger to Watch
A bull steepening, with the 2Y falling faster than the 10Y as cuts get priced, would cut the opportunity cost of holding bullion; official-sector buying sets the floor, and real yields set the pace.

crypto.title: Bitcoin absorbs the Binance shock while the ETF trade tightens GBTC
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 37,289.62 USD, down 0.38% on the day but up 7.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2023-11-23). Ether at 2,062.21 USD is up 12.52% over 20 sessions and 5.04% over five, and Solana's 43.22% 20-session gain makes it the speculative leader. The market shrugged off Binance: Fortune reported BNB dropping on criminal charges as bitcoin dipped only slightly [[n0880]], and Reuters then reported bitcoin rising 5.7% to $37,802 [[n0888]]. Forbes notes bitcoin is up 120% this year [[n0887]], and the rally is broadening into meme tokens, with BONK up 25% on a Binance listing [[n0891]].
New / Most Important

The US settlement removes a systemic overhang rather than adding one. Former chief executive CZ was released on a $175M bond as prosecutors seek to review the terms [[n0886]], and Richard Teng takes over as CEO [[n0893]]. The ETF trade is tightening: GBTC's discount to NAV fell below 10% for the first time in two years [[n0898]], and BlackRock reportedly met the SEC over its spot bitcoin ETF [[n0889]]. Regulation is tightening at the retail edge, as Singapore will bar local credit cards for crypto purchases [[n1631]], while OKX became the first major exchange to apply for a Hong Kong licence [[n1614]].
Playbook

Action: hold core bitcoin exposure and express ETF optionality through GBTC's narrowing discount rather than high-beta altcoins. Coinbase, up 40.44% over 20 sessions to 109.25 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), already prices a lot, and Yahoo Finance argues its valuation is getting ahead of itself [[n0813]]. Trigger: a formal SEC decision on spot ETFs. Risk: any reversal in the Binance settlement terms, or a dollar rebound that drains speculative liquidity.

flows.title: Liquidity is loosening through rates and the dollar, not central banks
parts: Global Liquidity

Global liquidity is easing through price rather than balance-sheet policy. The 10Y Treasury yield dropped 53 bps over 20 observations to 4.42% (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-22), and the DXY fell 2.45% to 103.92 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), loosening financial conditions worldwide without a single rate cut. The Fed's own plumbing remains restrictive: the St. Louis Fed explains the 'deferred asset' that builds while the Fed's remittances to the Treasury are suspended [[n1017]], a reminder that balance-sheet run-off continues regardless of rate talk. Liquidity is also being built bilaterally — the PBOC's $7 billion swap line with Saudi Arabia [[n0204]] — and the FT notes EM central banks may already be ahead of the Fed and the ECB [[n1129]].
Rates & Dollar

The dollar's slide is broad. InvestmentNews reported the dollar down further on rates speculation [[n1113]], and jobless claims boosted Fed rate-cut bets [[n1834]]. But the minutes argue rates need to stay high [[n0606]], so the market is pricing cuts the Fed has not endorsed. The DXY's 0.32% rise in its latest session as gold slipped below $2,000 [[n1880]] shows how quickly that can reverse. Three-month bills at 5.54% still pay more than the 10Y at 4.42%, and ETF.com's look beyond TLT to short-term Treasury ETFs [[n1164]] reflects that preference for cash-like duration; TLT has nonetheless gained 8.89% over 20 sessions to 90.87 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22).
Credit Check

Credit is priced for a soft landing. HYG rose 3.99% over 20 sessions to 75.08 USD and LQD 6.23% to 105.26 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), and Morningstar's list of top-performing high-yield corporate bond funds [[n1149]] signals performance chasing. The cracks sit outside US corporate credit: the ECB warns euro-zone banks are starting to show stress as defaults rise [[n1134]], the St. Louis Fed maps commercial-real-estate risks [[n1146]], and China's Zhongzhi admitted a £30bn shortfall [[n0249]]. Weak credits are still finding buyers — the AFR notes coal miners discovering nobody will judge them in the bond market [[n1915]] — which is late-cycle behaviour rather than a stress signal.
Equity & Fund Flows

Positioning is the binding constraint. Goldman says hedge-fund bets on US stocks are the most crowded ever [[n0615]], retail investors crowded into Eli Lilly after the weight-loss drug approval [[n0337]], and a BofA survey ranks Japan and India as the most favoured markets in Asia-Pacific [[n1147]]. The hedge-fund industry is shrinking at the edges: Jim Chanos is closing his funds after 38 years [[n1584]], and Tiger Global's Scott Shleifer has stepped down [[n0847]]. Capital markets are trying to widen the funnel: Hong Kong's exchange launched a digital IPO platform to boost listings [[n1162]], and Euronews describes a great delisting of European companies toward US exchanges [[n0843]], which concentrates liquidity further in New York.
Portfolio Implication

Crowding plus a VIX at 12.85 index points means volatility is the cheapest hedge in the book: buy index protection while it is inexpensive instead of selling winners. Keep credit at benchmark because spreads already price the soft landing, and use cash at 5.54% as the funding leg for duration in the belly. Rotation candidates are the underowned: small caps, EM dollar debt and Polish banks, each of which gains if the dollar keeps sliding. The signal that liquidity is tightening again is a DXY move back toward 106.53 index points, its level 20 sessions ago; that would argue for cutting EM and small-cap exposure first.

anticipatory.title: OPEC+ after the delay: a cut the market does not believe
parts: What Is Priced

WTI's 9.71% 20-session fall to 77.10 USD/bbl and USO's 8.73% decline (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22) price an OPEC+ that cannot agree. CNN tied oil's 4% drop to the delay of the meeting [[n1737]], while OilPrice argues the Middle East is enjoying its last month of high prices before cuts kick in [[n1693]].
Conditional Expression

If the group agrees deeper, enforced cuts, the asymmetry favours under-owned energy equities: XLE at 84.58 USD after a 3.22% 20-session fall, and Brent-linked majors such as Shell, down 3.81% over 20 sessions. If it fails again, the expression is long duration and airlines, as lower oil feeds lower inflation expectations and a flatter curve.
Risk

Supply outside the group can swamp either outcome: Venezuela says it is producing 850,000 bpd and wants back US share [[n1046]]. Red Sea shipping risk after the Houthis seized a cargo ship and named Israeli vessels legitimate targets [[n1209]] can add a premium regardless of what OPEC+ decides.

anticipatory.title: Fed: the market's cut timetable versus the minutes
parts: What Is Priced

The 2Y at 4.89%, 19 bps lower over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2023-11-22), prices a peak, and jobless claims have boosted rate-cut bets [[n1834]]. Forbes lays out the Fed's 2024 meeting schedule and rate outlook [[n1918]], and the market has effectively front-loaded easing into that calendar.
Conditional Expression

If the next inflation prints confirm October's flat CPI [[n1825]], own the belly through the 5Y at 4.44% and add small caps on the 2Y breaking lower. If the minutes' higher-for-longer stance [[n0606]] is reinforced by a hot print, flatten duration, hold cash at 5.54% and favour quality balance sheets over leveraged cyclicals.
Risk

The bullish case can arrive for the wrong reason. Fannie Mae's call for a mild 2024 recession [[n1888]] and the Conference Board's warning of a very short recession [[n1927]] describe cuts delivered alongside falling earnings, which would help bonds and hurt the crowded equity leaders.

anticipatory.title: Spot bitcoin ETF decision
parts: What Is Priced

GBTC's discount below 10% [[n0898]] and bitcoin's 7.36% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2023-11-23) price a high probability of approval. The New York Times linked the latest surge directly to the prospect of a bitcoin fund [[n0858]].
Conditional Expression

Approval: the GBTC discount should close and listed proxies re-rate further — MicroStrategy at 507.88 USD, up 17.23% over 20 sessions, and Riot, up 8.61% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22). Delay or denial: the high-beta proxies fall hardest, so a long bitcoin, short proxy-basket position isolates the decision risk.
Risk

Retail-access rules are tightening elsewhere: CNBC reports Singapore will tighten crypto rules for retail customers [[n0903]]. Politics adds noise, with Politico describing a crypto super PAC trying to swing 2024 [[n0875]], which can turn a technical decision into a political one.

anticipatory.title: Poland's handover and the first EU money
parts: What Is Priced

EPOL's 13.14% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22) and a zloty at its strongest in years [[n1355]] price a smooth handover and fast EU money; Interia says the first large transfers arrive in January [[n1471]].
Conditional Expression

If the Tusk government takes office on schedule and submits the budget, as Gazeta Prawna expects [[n1561]], add Polish banks — PKO and Pekao — and hold the zloty. If the State Tribunal threat against Glapiński [[n1411]] escalates into an open institutional clash, hedge the currency and rotate from banks toward exporters that benefit from a weaker zloty.
Risk

The EU billions are not unconditional [[n1555]], and Kotecki's warning that Poland runs the EU's second-highest deficit [[n1354]] means the Commission can slow money just as pay pledges raise spending.

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA): record quarter meets a crowded tape
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia reported record revenue and earnings in fiscal Q3 [[n1010]], and the WSJ sees no end in sight for the AI boom [[n1039]]. Data-center demand plus sovereign AI clouds keeps estimates rising faster than the share price.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock fell 2.46% to 487.16 USD after the print, still up 16.60% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22). Bloomberg framed it as a test of whether great is good enough after a $240 billion rally [[n0991]]; China export restrictions are the main earnings risk.
Trade Expression
Accumulate on post-earnings weakness rather than chase; a retest of 417.79 USD, the level 20 sessions ago, would be the add zone. Use call spreads to cap premium while implied volatility stays low.

catalysts.title: Deere (DE): the farm cycle turns
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Deere's 2024 guidance missed estimates and the shares tumbled [[n0715]], even as fiscal-year net income surged despite a fourth-quarter sales dip [[n0714]]. Peak earnings are behind it as farm incomes normalise.
Price Hurdle & Risk

DE fell 3.11% to 370.76 USD and is down 0.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22) while industrials rallied 8.57%. Soybeans down 1.51% in the latest session add pressure. The risk to the short is buybacks and a fast rebound in crop prices.
Trade Expression
Underweight versus XLI, or pair short DE against long Caterpillar, which held up better over 20 sessions. Cover if DE reclaims 371.91 USD, its level 20 sessions ago, on improving dealer orders.

catalysts.title: Alibaba (BABA): the governance discount deepens
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The cloud spin-off U-turn lopped $20 billion off Alibaba's market value [[n0182]], and Jack Ma backed off plans to sell shares after the plunge [[n0826]]. The thesis now rests on buybacks and core e-commerce cash, not on unlocking value.
Price Hurdle & Risk

BABA fell 9.31% over five sessions to 78.96 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22), and the Hong Kong line is down 3.13% over 20 sessions while Tencent rose 14.46%. Analysts' target cuts of up to 25% [[n0444]] reset expectations lower.
Trade Expression
Neutral: prefer Tencent as the China platform long. Revisit Alibaba only if management lays out a credible new restructuring path or a materially larger capital return.

catalysts.title: Novo Nordisk (NVO): capacity is the catalyst
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Macron was set to unveil a 2.1 billion euro Novo investment in France [[n0745]], and Novo will cut Victoza output to boost Ozempic supply [[n1745]]. Supply, not demand, limits earnings, so every capacity step converts into revenue.
Price Hurdle & Risk

NVO rose 7.08% over five sessions to 103.26 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22); the Copenhagen line closed at 709.30 DKK (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-23). Risks are pricing politics and compounded copies of the drug, plus Lilly's competing capacity build.
Trade Expression
Own Novo over consumer staples exposed to GLP-1 volume loss; add on pullbacks toward 97.43 USD, the ADR's level 20 sessions ago.

catalysts.title: Tesla (TSLA): Cybertruck event versus brand damage
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Tesla will deliver only 10 Cybertrucks at its big event this month, an executive said [[n1015]], so the launch is symbolic rather than material. Meanwhile, Musk's social-media comments have sparked an investor backlash [[n1622]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

TSLA fell 2.90% to 234.21 USD and is down 3.55% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22). Swedish dockworkers refusing to unload Teslas [[n1658]] add labour risk in Europe. Upside risk is a strong Cybertruck reception.
Trade Expression
Underweight versus the Nasdaq 100; use the Cybertruck event as a liquidity window to reduce. Reassess only if price cuts stop and margins stabilise.

catalysts.title: Palantir (PLTR): the NHS contract
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Palantir won an NHS data contract worth up to £480 million [[n0645]], a marquee civilian win that validates its push beyond defence, and Barron's said the stock was on pace for its highest close in two years [[n0329]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

PLTR closed at 19.69 USD, up 26.30% over 20 sessions but down 1.30% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2023-11-22). The Guardian reports patient-privacy fears around the £330m contract [[n0646]], which could slow roll-out.
Trade Expression
Hold, do not chase: momentum is extended after a 20-session run. Add only on a pullback toward 15.59 USD, the level 20 sessions ago, or on evidence of additional government data wins.
